clue.text: No hope of French couple's son getting ahead

indicators.note: getting ahead tells us the son is placed in front of the couple rather than after it

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
S is the standard abbreviation for son
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A French couple's son forging ahead in life leaves nobody any hope of catching him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of French' asks for the French word for 'of'; the son jumps the queue and stands before the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the state of having lost all hope, so the noun matches the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Water down some Lucozade at first in miserable diet

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside the other
a miserable diet is a wretched, badly made one, so its letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the first part of the drink's name, its opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone on a joyless diet thins their glass of Lucozade, a British fizzy energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucozade is a British glucose energy drink. Only a portion of its name is wanted: the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a liquid is to weaken it by adding water, the phrasal verb's exact sense.

clue.text: Grab top spot, naturally!

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the top letter of spot
natch is informal slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: Someone jubilantly seizing first place, as if it were only their due.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to seize something quickly, a direct synonym of the verb grab.

clue.text: Come what may, a high street's secured by companies

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it

parts.note: taken as written
high and tall are synonyms
Co is the abbreviation for company, plural Cos
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A commentator insists firms will snap up a high street whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The street's abbreviation sits inside the companies' plural abbreviation, between CO and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms meaning regardless of the consequences or whatever happens.

clue.text: Go over to put a new hat on?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read whimsically: give a fresh cap, re- plus cap

explanation.surface: Someone crossing the room to try on a different hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, where the word splits as RE (again) and CAP (hat).
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to restate the main points, and a re-cap would literally be a hat fitted afresh.

clue.text: Play on words has some Morse code for experts

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
dits are the short signals, the dots, in Morse code

explanation.surface: A wordplay puzzle that happens to contain Morse, set as a challenge for specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Pundits are learned authorities who offer opinions in the media, a synonym for experts.

clue.text: Invite pal round, when unhappy

indicators.note: turning the words round invites a new order for their letters

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Advice to have a friend over whenever you are feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaintive means sounding sad or mournful, close enough to unhappy as an adjective.

clue.text: Old boatbuilder's working up one final berth

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a means one

indicators.note: final asks for only the last letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of berth

explanation.surface: An old shipwright is busy finishing off one last bunk on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Berth and boatbuilder conjure a dockyard; the biblical ark builder is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this patriarch built the ark, so he is the archetypal ancient boatbuilder.

clue.text: They win a throw by causing obstruction

indicators.note: to throw something is to scatter it, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A team won a match by deliberately blocking opponents, as in a wrestling throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in the way is an obstacle, so it is blocking or impeding progress.

clue.text: Gentleman's award is reported with amazement

indicators.note: something reported is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: a knight's title, sir, followed by a prize

explanation.surface: News of a knight's honour is greeted with astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir is the title for a gentleman, a knight; said aloud with prize it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprise is the feeling of astonishment at the unexpected, a synonym of amazement.

clue.text: Before lunch everybody comes back to see this animal

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: am is the morning, the time before noon
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A morning trip where the whole group returns to view a zoo creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal of the camel family, kept for wool and as a pack beast.

clue.text: Symbol of courage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a letter or sign used in writing

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as an emblem of bravery; split it into two separate meanings joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a written sign, such as a letter, and strength of personality or fortitude.

clue.text: Softly stroke flower with delight

parts.note: to tickle is to touch lightly
the pink is a garden flower, a kind of dianthus

explanation.surface: Gently caressing a bloom, with obvious pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With delight' looks like an adverb phrase for the stroking; 'with' only links. To be tickled pink is to be thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: To tickle someone pink is to please them enormously, an idiomatic verb meaning to delight.

clue.text: Feel scared by loud organ!

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by a booming church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The church organ is a false scent: the organ is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear something is to be afraid of it, so the verb matches the phrase.

clue.text: Spies conceal cock-up ere M arrives with contracts

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside

parts.note: spies are secret agents

indicators.note: a cock-up is a botched job, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Secret agents cover up a blunder before their chief M turns up with the paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories, which makes the spy scene vivid.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracts are legally binding agreements between parties, the plural noun in both cases.

clue.text: For getting on plane: directors get in first, then doctor, then an American behind

parts.note: a company's directors form its board
taken as written
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
ass is the American word for the backside

explanation.surface: Boarding order on a flight: the bosses first, then the doctor, then an American at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the answer is the thing you need for getting on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarding pass is the card or document allowing a traveller onto an aircraft.

clue.text: Artist runs line through space and time

indicators.note: one thing running through others passes into their middle

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
an em is a printer's unit of space
a brand is a product line
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sci-fi traveller drawing a line across the space-time continuum.
explanation.walkthrough: The product line sits between the printer's space and time's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great Dutch painter of the seventeenth century, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Distress for Rhode Island woman under gag order

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming after in the answer
putting something in a new order rearranges its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock woman

explanation.surface: A woman from Rhode Island is upset by a court's gagging order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag order' reads as a legal injunction, but 'order' is the rearranging signal for the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to cause someone pain or a sense of injustice, a verb synonym of distress.

clue.text: Toilet initially gets put on building site that's most muddy!

indicators.note: in a down clue, something put on another sits above it

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement
initially takes just the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of gets
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A portable loo is set up on a building site, which is the muddiest place around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building site' looks like one phrase; 'building' is the signal and 'site' its fodder. Bog is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggiest is the superlative of boggy, meaning wet and marshy, so it is the muddiest.

clue.text: Kind of blush about poem Ted composed

indicators.note: about means around, so one part wraps round the other

parts.note: to go red is to blush

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy poet named Ted reddens at a verse he has written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like vague hedging; 'Kind' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-tempered person is pleasant and amiable, an adjective close to kind.

clue.text: Tried to point to overt mismanagement

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point

indicators.note: mismanagement throws things into disorder, so the word's letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone made an effort to highlight blatant incompetence in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to make great efforts, so it means attempted.

clue.text: Poles secure Native American panel

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, here between two outer letters

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: Polish negotiators lock in a Native American seat on an advisory board.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a partition or flat board used to divide a space, a kind of panel.

clue.text: Fashion for old cloth's elegant, initially

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of old cloth

indicators.note: initially keeps just the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of elegant

explanation.surface: A fashion world where vintage fabric is suddenly chic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a verb; it is the noun, as in all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a craze, the latest trend everyone wants, as in the phrase all the rage.

clue.text: Working out numbers for crime, hit at corruption

indicators.note: corruption spoils and distorts, so the letters are twisted into a different order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A forensic accountant tallies figures to strike at crime and graft.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic is the branch of mathematics dealing with calculating with numbers.

clue.text: Bust myth associated with energy-giving herb

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so its letters are smashed and reset

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Debunking the claim that a certain herb gives you a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy-giving' reads as one compound adjective; split it, as 'energy' supplies a letter and 'giving' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic plant of the mint family used in cooking, so it is a herb.

clue.text: Giant dog reeks a bit

indicators.note: a bit means a piece, so the letters are a section lifted from the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A huge hound has a whiff about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore and fairy tales.

clue.text: English come together with bearing, outwardly cheery in crisis

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
to merge is to come together
N, north, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: outwardly keeps just the outside letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of cheery

explanation.surface: An English team stays cheerful on the surface while uniting in a moment of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation that needs urgent action, a synonym of crisis.

clue.text: Drug, in the near future, is about to become a rope around your neck

indicators.note: turning about means facing the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
soon means in the near future

explanation.surface: A warning that drug use will soon land you on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to become' reads as one phrase meaning soon; 'about' is the signal and 'to become' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot, as used for hanging someone by the neck.

clue.text: Petition hospital department about bringing back volunteers

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A petition to a hospital ward asking it to reinstate its volunteer helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, the Territorial Army, is the British army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or beg, which is what it means to petition someone.

clue.text: Religious festival's name is oriental

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival of the resurrection
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A claim that a religious feast's title comes from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern and oriental both describe things from or relating to the East, especially Asia.
